newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares race ahead, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares race ahead, more gains seen.

text.p: Austrian shares stormed to their highest close since June 26 on Friday as October futures and options expired and traders said an assault on resistance at 1,100 points was on the cards.
"We can really attack 1,100 now," one said.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares climbed to an intraday high of 1,099.86, before easing to close 3.2 points or 0.29 percent firmer at 1,093.
Overall 10 ATX shares rose, 10 fell and one remained unchanged.

Traders said news that Investmentbank Austria's head trader had been barred had little impact on proceedings. The move by the stock exchange followed a last minute sell-off that hammered the ATX on October 16.

The Vienna bourse also announced plans to introduce a weighted close for ATX shares and raise the minimum trading volume for market makers in an effort to reduce the risk of big price movements in late trade.
"The changes are probably a good idea but by barring one trader they are just looking for a scapegoat," a dealer said.
Bank Austria, which owns Investmentbank Austria, later announced it was parting company with the trader. Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa is also president of the Vienna bourse.
The October ATX future added 11.3 points to expire at 1,095.5. Traders said the expiry went smoothly.
The leading gainer was ATX heavyweight EA Generali. Shares in the insurer jumped 125 schillings to 3,310.
Luxury hosiery maker Wolford was the leading decliner, tumbling 29 schillings to 1,470.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index rose 2.82 points or 0.68 percent to 419.16
